source._builder_note: Since 2026-10-10 the build stage is ubuntu:24.04 (the runtime's own distro) with the build_packages below, and the Rust 1.98.1 toolchain copied from the pinned rust:1.98.1-bookworm image (rustup's portable x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu dist; no official rust image is built on Ubuntu). cargo vendor, source_prep and post_vendor_cmds still run in the rust image online (CARGO_HOME=/usr/local/cargo there, as post_vendor_cmds expects). Native crates at v3.12.0 (Cargo.lock): ring, psm, croaring-sys, zstd-sys and tikv-jemalloc-sys compile bundled C with cc/make; liblzma-sys links a system liblzma only at >= 5.8.0 (noble has 5.6.1, bookworm had 5.4.1), so it builds its bundled xz in both; bzip2 is libbz2-rs-sys (Rust); flate2 has no libz-sys; libsqlite3-sys is bundled (the bookworm runtime carried no libsqlite3 and booted). rust:bookworm baked gcc/g++/make; on ubuntu:24.04 they come from build-essential.
source._toolchain_note: rust-toolchain.toml pins channel 1.98.1 with rustfmt/clippy/rust-analyzer/rust-src - exactly the builder's toolchain. The offline build stage sets RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.98.1 (source.rust_toolchain), which stops rustup trying to download the listed components under --network=none (the vaultwarden trap). Edition 2024 (Cargo.toml:134).
source._features_note: Default features: jemalloc_replacing_malloc, azure, gcp, aws, large-strings (influxdb3/Cargo.toml [features]). large-strings only raises the line-protocol string field limit from 64 KiB to 1 MiB (core/influxdb_line_protocol/src/lib.rs:105-112). Upstream's Dockerfile builds --no-default-features with aws,gcp,azure,jemalloc_replacing_malloc (Dockerfile:18); CI checks the prod-image feature set WITH large-strings (.circleci/config.yml:431). The Rust renderer cannot pass --no-default-features, so this build keeps the crate defaults. tokio_console is NOT enabled.
source._build_env_note: GIT_HASH/GIT_HASH_SHORT: influxdb3_process/build.rs reads them, else runs `git rev-parse HEAD` and PANICS ('attempting to embed empty git hash') - the vendor stage deletes .git. The values appear in `influxdb3 --version` ('InfluxDB 3 Core, <ver>, revision <sha>', influxdb3_process/src/lib.rs:31-38) and in /ping. RUSTFLAGS: upstream's .cargo/config.toml passes `--cfg tokio_unstable` (plus lld, target-cpu=haswell and frame pointers); the Rust vendor stage OVERWRITES that file with the cargo-vendor source replacement, so tokio_unstable is restored here. target-cpu=haswell is deliberately NOT restored: upstream's binaries need AVX2, this one runs on any x86-64. PYO3_PYTHON: pyo3 is a hard dependency (influxdb3_processing_engine/Cargo.toml:34); upstream links it against python-build-standalone 3.13.15 downloaded in its Dockerfile (.circleci/scripts/fetch-python-standalone.bash). This build links Ubuntu 24.04's CPython 3.12 instead (python3-dev at build, libpython3.12t64 at run time; it was bookworm's 3.11 before 2026-10-10): a distro package we vendor as debs, not a prebuilt tarball. pyo3 0.29 supports 3.12.
source_prep: B=core/iox_query_udf/build.rs && D=target/cfg_independent_downloads/iox_query_udf && grep -q 'join("cfg_independent_downloads")' $B && grep -q 'join("iox_query_udf")' $B && C=$(sed -n 's/^const COMMIT: &str = "\([0-9a-f]\{40\}\)";$/\1/p' $B) && T=$(sed -n 's/^const BUILD_TIMESTAMP: &str = "\(.*\)";$/\1/p' $B | sed 's/+00:00$//; s/:/-/g') && S=$(sed -n 's/^ *"sha256:\([0-9a-f]\{64\}\)";$/\1/p' $B) && test -n "$C" && test -n "$T" && test -n "$S" && U="https://github.com/influxdata/datafusion-udf-wasm/releases/download/wasm-binaries%2F$T%2F$C" && F=datafusion_udf_wasm_python.release.x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.elf && mkdir -p $D && curl -fsSL --retry 5 -o $D/sha256sum.txt "$U/sha256sum.txt" && echo "$S  $D/sha256sum.txt" | sha256sum -c - && curl -fsSL --retry 5 -o "$D/$F" "$U/$F" && (cd $D && grep "  $F\$" sha256sum.txt | sha256sum -c -)
source._source_prep_note: Emitted by render_l009_rust_kit since 879fd93; chain 488's vendor stage ran it (both files landed in vendored/influxdb-src/target/cfg_independent_downloads/iox_query_udf/ on <redacted: internal host>, ELF 90,861,736 bytes). It reads COMMIT, BUILD_TIMESTAMP and SHA256_TXT_CHECKSUM from core/iox_query_udf/build.rs itself (so a retarget follows upstream's own pins automatically), downloads sha256sum.txt and checks it against upstream's pinned checksum, then downloads datafusion_udf_wasm_python.release.x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.elf and checks it against sha256sum.txt. At v3.12.0 that is release 'wasm-binaries/2026-08-24T15-37-49/171fb474...' (built with wasmtime 48.0.0; Cargo.lock has 48.0.1), sha256sum.txt a25fec27067332f63cd342e5a87967b0848d836124387a0d9f48f7b56fc99fd7 (downloaded and verified 2026-10-04) and the ELF 7f951ba7f55c0e6ecaa7ebffcf02debbb9e73eb5764f9d47db62c27b52eab299 (90,861,736 bytes). Both files go to target/cfg_independent_downloads/iox_query_udf/ - the directory v3.12.0's build.rs computes from OUT_DIR (get_cargo_target_dir(): four levels up = <target-dir>, which is /src/target in the offline stage) - so fetch_artifact() finds them with matching checksums and never touches the network. No source file is modified; the grep guards fail the vendor stage if upstream moves that directory again (v3.11.4 used OUT_DIR/iox_query_udf_download). HONEST DISCLOSURE: this ELF is the ONE prebuilt binary in the image - an InfluxData-built, wasmtime-precompiled CPython guest for Python SQL UDFs. Upstream's release page itself says pre-built binaries require you to validate the source and trust the binary. It is pinned by checksum and comes from the same upstream organisation at the commit the source names (the qdrant-web-ui precedent), but it is not compiled by us and Scout cannot see the CPython inside it. Building it from source needs wasi-sdk, a CPython WASI build and the wasm32-wasip2 Rust target - a separate toolchain project. Checked 2026-10-04 by running the rendered command with /bin/sh (dash) in a v3.12.0 checkout: both `sha256sum -c` checks passed and the files landed in target/cfg_independent_downloads/iox_query_udf/. Measured 2026-10-04: `cargo check --offline --locked -p iox_query_udf` with --network=none in the rendered cargovendor stage finished (exit 0), so build.rs found both files offline and include_bytes! resolved; the release build is the same lookup (OUT_DIR four levels below /src/target).
post_vendor_cmds: H=vendor/datafusion-udf-wasm-host/src/bindings.rs && grep -q 'path: "../wit/world.wit"' $H && R=$(sed -n 's|^source = "git+https://github.com/influxdata/datafusion-udf-wasm.git?rev=[0-9a-f]*#\([0-9a-f]\{40\}\)"$|\1|p' Cargo.lock | sort -u) && test "$(echo $R | wc -w)" = 1 && W=$(echo ${CARGO_HOME:-/usr/local/cargo}/git/checkouts/datafusion-udf-wasm-*/$(echo $R | cut -c1-7)) && test "$(git -C "$W" rev-parse HEAD)" = "$R" && test -f "$W/wit/world.wit" && test ! -e vendor/wit && cp -R "$W/wit" vendor/wit && echo "post_vendor: vendor/wit from datafusion-udf-wasm@$R" && ls -l vendor/wit
source._post_vendor_note: Chain 488's scratch build failed (exit 101, 507 s in) compiling datafusion-udf-wasm-host: `failed to read path for WIT [/src/vendor/datafusion-udf-wasm-host/../wit/world.wit] No such file or directory` (+ 11 follow-on errors). That crate is a GIT dependency (Cargo.toml:269, influxdata/datafusion-udf-wasm rev 9186474d) whose src/bindings.rs:4-8 runs wasmtime's `bindgen!({ path: "../wit/world.wit" })` - a file at that repo's WORKSPACE ROOT, outside the crate. Upstream builds from cargo's full git checkout, where ../wit exists; `cargo vendor` copies only the crate's package directory, so vendored it resolves to vendor/wit/world.wit, which nothing creates. This command runs in the online vendor stage right after `cargo vendor` (render_l009_rust_kit, source.post_vendor_cmds) and copies wit/ from the checkout cargo vendor itself just made - the same tree the vendored host crate came from - after checking that bindings.rs still reads ../wit/world.wit, that Cargo.lock pins exactly one datafusion-udf-wasm rev, and that the checkout's HEAD is that rev (it reads the rev from Cargo.lock, so a retarget follows upstream's pin). Cargo's directory source ignores vendor/ subdirectories without a Cargo.toml, so vendor/wit is inert to cargo; no vendored file or .cargo-checksum.json changes. wit/ at 9186474d is the single self-contained world.wit (package datafusion-udf-wasm:udf@0.5.0, no foreign `use`; sha256 b0da509c...). Swept the other git dependencies the same way: the 33 DataFusion-fork crates (influxdata/arrow-datafusion 676dd338) and the other two udf-wasm crates have no include_str!/include_bytes!/include!/bindgen path outside their package; datafusion-proto(-common) exclude *.proto but compile only checked-in generated .rs. MEASURED 2026-10-04 on the agent VM (not a prep host): built the rendered Dockerfile.vendor cargovendor stage (legacy builder) - every guard passed and it logged 'post_vendor: vendor/wit from datafusion-udf-wasm@9186474d...'; then, in that image with --network=none, `cargo check --offline --locked -p iox_query_udf` (covers datafusion-udf-wasm-host) finished in 4m32s, exit 0. Control, same image with vendor/wit removed: `cargo check -p datafusion-udf-wasm-host` exits 101 with chain 488's exact error. The full release build (fat LTO, link) was not run here.
